title: Week of Aug 17–23 · Emma's Kickoff
subtitle: Welcome, Emma! You kicked things off with Thursday's 4-mile run. Log it below, then Day 1 proper is tonight's strength session.
goals: Log Thursday's 4-mile run (time, effort, and how the IT band felt). That note drives next week
First strength session tonight (Fri). Start light, form first: Back Squat at your 65 lb, RPE 6–7, a couple reps in the tank
Start the hip + glute work. Small moves now are what keep the IT band happy as your running builds
Saturday: short and easy — a 1.5–2 mi easy run, a bike ride, or a Sculpt class all count. Sunday: gentle stretch
One-time setup: connect Strava at workoutplanning-production.up.railway.app/api/strava/connect/emma so your runs and heart rate show up here automatically
review: Welcome to your plan! Your 8 weeks point at two things: getting stronger and becoming a better runner, with Yoga Sculpt staying in the mix because you love it. This weekend is a kickoff, and your first full week (Mon/Tue/Wed/Thu/Sat evenings, ~60 min) starts Monday. One honest note on Thursday: 4 miles is a big day against a ~6 mile week, so the next couple of runs stay short and easy on purpose. Because the IT band aches during and after runs right now, the first 2–3 weeks keep runs short (1.5–2.5 mi), lean on the bike for extra cardio (every run card has a 🚴 swap), and put a heavy dose of glute and hip strength on every lifting day. Stronger hips + patient volume is the standard fix for IT band trouble, and your Yoga Sculpt classes count as plan days, so total volume stays sane. Lifting starts from what you know: Back Squat at 65 lb, RPE 6–7, and we progress from whatever you log. On weight: the goal is maintaining ~138 while adding muscle — your Weight page has your own calorie and protein targets. Light nutrition tip to start: since snacking is the main pattern, anchor a protein source at each meal and keep easy snacks visible, e.g. Greek yogurt, fruit, jerky. Log everything, even one line on how it felt. Next week builds from what you actually did.

run.detail: Two days after a 4-miler with a cranky IT band, this is deliberately small: 1.5–2 miles at a pace where you could chat the whole way (walk breaks totally fine). If the IT band complains at all, tap the 🚴 toggle and ride easy instead — the bike gives the cardio without the impact. A Sculpt class also counts as today's session; just log it in the notes. Whatever you pick, note how the IT band responded.
